objectives: Describe the job of each specialised cell
Explain how a cell's features help it do its job

questions.q: What does MRS GREN stand for?
questions.a: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition.

questions.q: Name three parts of a light microscope.
questions.a: Any three: eyepiece lens, objective lens, stage, focus knob, light, arm, base.

questions.q: Name four parts found in an animal cell.
Name the three extra parts in a plant cell.
What is the job of the nucleus?
questions.a: Controls the cell and holds the genetic material.
Respiration, which releases energy for the cell.

engage.hook: You can spot a doctor, a lifeguard or a hairdresser just by looking at them. What gives their job away?
engage.imageDescription: doctor holding a stethoscope towards the camera

reveal.answer: Their kit fits their job: a stethoscope, a float, a hairdryer. Cells work the same way. A cell's shape and parts give away the job it does.

learn.heading: What is a specialised cell?

items: A cell with special features, called adaptations, that help it do one job.
Most still have the parts from last lesson: nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria.
Link every feature to the job: "It has ___ so that it can ___."
Your body has around 200 kinds of cell, and they all came from one fertilised egg cell.

learn.imageDescription: group of specialised cells: nerve, sperm, egg, red blood, ciliated, palisade and root hair cells

learn.heading: Cell laminates

items: Visit each cell laminate around the room.
For each cell, write where it is found, its job and its special features in the table on your worksheet.
Sperm, egg, red blood cell, nerve cell, ciliated cell, root hair cell, palisade cell.

learn.imageDescription: blank specialised cells table with columns for where found, job and special features

learn.heading: Specialised animal cells

comparison.bTitle: Special features and how they help

rows.a: Sperm cell: carries the father's genes
rows.b: Tail to swim. Lots of mitochondria for energy. Enzymes in the head to get into the egg.

rows.a: Egg cell: carries the mother's genes
rows.b: Large, with a food store for the new cell. Jelly coat lets only one sperm in.
No nucleus, so more room for haemoglobin to carry oxygen. Flexible, to fit through capillaries.
Long, to carry signals a long way. Branches connect to other cells.

rows.a: Ciliated cell: keeps the airways clean
rows.b: Cilia sweep mucus, dust and bacteria up and out of the lungs.

learn.imageDescription: red blood cell diagram showing its dimpled disc shape

learn.heading: Specialised plant cells

items: Job: absorb water and minerals from the soil.
Long, thin hair gives a large surface area, so more water is absorbed.
No chloroplasts: there is no light underground.
Job: photosynthesis, making food for the plant.
Packed with chloroplasts to absorb lots of light.
Tall and thin, so many fit at the top of the leaf where the light is.

learn.imageDescription: root hair cell diagram with long thin hair, vacuole and thin cell wall

build.q: Which cell has a tail so it can swim to another cell?
options: Egg cell
Sperm cell
Nerve cell
Ciliated cell
build.explanation: The sperm cell swims to the egg using its tail.

build.q: Why does a red blood cell have no nucleus?
options: So it can swim faster
So it can absorb more water
So it can carry electrical signals
So it has more room to carry oxygen
build.explanation: With no nucleus there is more room for haemoglobin, which carries oxygen.

build.q: Which cell is packed with chloroplasts?
options: Palisade cell
Root hair cell
Red blood cell
Egg cell
build.explanation: Palisade cells sit at the top of the leaf and absorb light for photosynthesis.

build.q: How do ciliated cells protect the lungs?
options: Their cilia make oxygen for the lungs
Their cilia soak dust into the cell
Their cilia sweep mucus out of the lungs
Their cilia sweep mucus into the lungs
build.explanation: Cilia sweep mucus, with trapped dust and bacteria, up and out of the lungs.

build.q: Why does a root hair cell have a long, thin hair?
options: To carry signals to the leaves
To give a large surface area to absorb water
To help it swim through the soil
To give a large surface area to absorb light
build.explanation: A large surface area means more water and minerals are absorbed from the soil.

build.q: Why is a nerve cell long?
options: To carry signals a long way
To store food for a new cell
To sweep mucus out of the lungs
To carry oxygen a long way
build.explanation: Nerve cells carry electrical signals from one part of the body to another.

statements.text: Specialised cells have no organelles at all.
statements.correction: Most still have a nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria. Red blood cells are unusual because they have no nucleus.

statements.text: An egg cell is much bigger than a sperm cell.
Root hair cells have lots of chloroplasts.
statements.correction: Root hair cells are underground with no light, so they have no chloroplasts.

statements.text: Mitochondria in a sperm cell release energy for swimming.
All the cells in your body look the same.
statements.correction: Cells have different shapes and features to suit their jobs.

developing.q: Job 1: sends electrical signals and has long branches. Which cell gets the job?
Job 3: likes sunlight and must have chloroplasts. Which cell gets the job?
Job 2 needs a food store for a new cell. Job 5 carries oxygen. Name both cells.
developing.a: Job 2: egg cell. Job 5: red blood cell.

reaching.q: Explain how a sperm cell's tail and mitochondria help it do its job.
reaching.a: The tail lets it swim to the egg. Mitochondria release energy for swimming.

reaching.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus. Explain why this helps it do its job.
reaching.a: There is more room for haemoglobin, so it can carry more oxygen.
starters: Without a nucleus there is more room for...

reaching.q: Reply to Job 4 (absorb water underground) as a root hair cell. Give two features and how each helps.
reaching.a: Long, thin hair gives a large surface area to absorb water and minerals. Thin cell wall lets water pass in easily.
starters: I have a ... so that I can ...

mastering.q: Write a CV for a ciliated cell: its job, where it works and how its features help.
mastering.a: Lines the airways. Cilia sweep mucus with dust and bacteria up and out of the lungs, keeping them clean.

mastering.q: Cells lining the gut have tiny folds. Suggest their job and how the folds help.
mastering.a: They absorb digested food into the blood. The folds give a large surface area, so food is absorbed faster.

mastering.q: Smoking stops cilia working. Explain why smokers cough more and get more infections.
mastering.a: Mucus with dust and bacteria is not swept out. It builds up, so they cough to clear it, and the bacteria cause infections.

cloze: A _____ cell has features that help it do one job.
A sperm cell has a _____ so it can swim to the egg.
A red blood cell has no _____, so it has more room to carry oxygen.
A root hair cell has a large surface _____ to absorb water.
Palisade cells are packed with _____ to absorb light.
Ciliated cells have tiny hairs called _____ that sweep mucus out of the lungs.
A nerve cell is long so it can carry electrical _____ around the body.
